intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
experiences.description: One of New Zealand's most iconic day hikes, crossing volcanic terrain with stunning views of emerald lakes and craters. Book an early shuttle from Queenstown or Wanaka to maximize daylight hours. Ideal for Day 2 or 3 after a rested arrival. Stay in Taupo or National Park Village the night before to avoid long morning transfers.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters, operated by AJ Hackett. Located just outside Queenstown, this is a must-do for adrenaline seekers. Book in advance to secure your preferred time slot. Stay in central Queenstown to minimize transfer time — the jump site is a short bus ride from town.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: A world-class Great Walk offering breathtaking alpine scenery through Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The Routeburn Falls and Lake Harris sections are accessible as a day hike. Stay in Glenorchy (45 min from Queenstown) the night before to catch the early morning trailhead shuttle and avoid wasted travel time.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Guided Walk and Cruise
experiences.description: Combine a guided nature walk along the Milford Track with a scenic cruise through Milford Sound's dramatic fiords and waterfalls. Depart from Te Anau (not Queenstown) to cut 1.5 hours off the transfer. Book accommodation in Te Anau the night before this activity to ensure an early, stress-free departure.

experiences.name: Ben Lomond Summit Hike
experiences.description: A challenging full-day hike directly accessible from central Queenstown, reaching 1,748 meters with panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. No transfers needed — the trailhead starts in town via the Skyline gondola area. Perfect for a mid-trip activity day when staying in central Queenstown, keeping costs and logistics minimal.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: A world-class Great Walk offering breathtaking alpine scenery through Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The Routeburn Falls and Lake Harris sections are accessible as a day hike. Stay in Glenorchy (45 min from Queenstown) the night before to catch the early morning trailhead shuttle and avoid wasted travel time.

experiences.name: Ben Lomond Summit Hike
experiences.description: A challenging full-day hike directly accessible from central Queenstown, reaching 1,748 meters with panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. No transfers needed — the trailhead starts in town via the Skyline gondola area. Perfect for a mid-trip activity day when staying in central Queenstown, keeping costs and logistics minimal.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 - nothing scheduled before arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Take the Connectabus (NZD ~$10) into central Queenstown. Check in to Queenstown Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk along the Queenstown Bay waterfront to get oriented. Stroll through the town centre and browse the shops along the Mall.
day_by_day.evening: Head up to Bob's Peak via the Queenstown Gondola (book online for ~NZD $32) or hike the free 45-minute track up for sunset panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. Return to town for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at Queenstown Airport on arrival
meals.lunch: Fergbaker on Shotover Street – iconic local bakery with hearty pies and sandwiches for under NZD $8
meals.dinner: Vudu Café & Larder on Rees Street – wholesome, affordable meals (mains ~NZD $18-22), great atmosphere for first evening

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the midday arrival. Pick up a free Queenstown map from the i-SITE Visitor Centre on Shotover Street. Buy a local SIM card (Skinny or 2degrees, ~NZD $20) at the airport or a convenience store for data and maps.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Ben Lomond Summit Hike – one of the best free hikes accessible directly from central Queenstown. Begin the trailhead near the Gondola base at 8:00am. The hike to the summit (1,748m) takes approximately 5-6 hours return. Enjoy stunning 360-degree views of Lake Wakatipu, the Remarkables, and Cecil Peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the descent back to Queenstown, arriving back in town by early-to-mid afternoon. Stop at the Gondola midway station on the way back for water. Rest tired legs back at the accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant lakefront. Visit Earnslaw Steamship Wharf area for free evening atmosphere. Grab dinner in town and plan tomorrow's activities.

meals.breakfast: Self-cater – pick up supplies from Pak'nSave supermarket (5-minute walk from central Queenstown) the night before. Oats, fruit, and toast. Budget ~NZD $5.
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch from Pak'nSave – sandwiches, muesli bars, fruit, and a reusable water bottle. Budget ~NZD $8.
meals.dinner: Winnies Gourmet Pizza on the Mall – great value pizzas from NZD $20, can be shared between two people

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is a strenuous hike – wear sturdy footwear, carry at least 2 litres of water, sunscreen, and layers as summit weather can change rapidly even in November. Start early to avoid afternoon cloud cover. This hike is completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning – sleep in and have a relaxed breakfast. Visit the Queenstown i-SITE to book the Routeburn Track Day Hike and confirm bungee jumping availability. Walk the free Queenstown Hill Time Walk (1.5 hours return) for gentle exercise and great town views – a perfect active recovery option.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungee (the world's first commercial bungee site, 43m drop). Take the free shuttle from central Queenstown. The jump costs ~NZD $165-185 – book online in advance for the best rate. Watch others jump for free if budget is tight, or commit to the iconic leap!
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungee jump with drinks and dinner on the waterfront. Browse the night markets if it's a Thursday (Queenstown Night Market runs Thursdays).

meals.breakfast: Self-cater at accommodation – eggs on toast, coffee. Budget ~NZD $4.
meals.lunch: Vudu Larder or Devil Burger on the Mall – great burgers from NZD $14-16
meals.dinner: The Cow Restaurant on Cow Lane – legendary Queenstown institution, affordable pasta and pizza in a cosy stone building, mains ~NZD $20-24

day_by_day.notes: Kawarau Bridge Bungee is the most affordable and historic of the Queenstown bungee options. Book at least 24 hours ahead online for a small discount. The free shuttle departs from central Queenstown – confirm times at i-SITE. Video packages are available but add significant cost (~NZD $50+) – optional for budget travellers.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Routeburn Track Day Hike. Depart Queenstown early (~7:00am) via Tracknet shuttle (~NZD $55 return) to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead near Glenorchy (1.5 hours). Hike the stunning Routeburn Track through beech forest, alongside the Routeburn River, and up to the Flats and Falls sections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking toward Routeburn Falls Hut (1,000m elevation) for breathtaking alpine views. Enjoy lunch at the hut lookout with views across the Humboldt Mountains. Begin the return hike back to the trailhead to meet the afternoon shuttle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown by early evening (~6:00-7:00pm). Rest, shower, and enjoy a quiet dinner. Legs will be tired – this is a 16-20km day depending on how far you hike.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at accommodation before departure – banana, peanut butter toast, coffee. Budget ~NZD $4.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Pak'nSave – wraps, trail mix, chocolate, and fruit. Budget ~NZD $8.
meals.dinner: Habebe on Church Street – Middle Eastern wraps and bowls, filling and affordable at ~NZD $15-18

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tracknet shuttle in advance at tracknet.net. The Routeburn Track is a Great Walk – the day hike sections do not require a Great Walk pass, but respect hut rules if stopping at Routeburn Falls Hut. Wear waterproof layers and sturdy boots. November weather can be unpredictable in Fiordland – check DOC weather forecasts the night before at doc.govt.nz.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day after two big hiking days. Sleep in, do laundry at the nearest laundromat (~NZD $8-10 wash and dry), and restock supplies at Pak'nSave. Visit the free Queenstown Gardens – a beautiful lakeside park with rose gardens and a disc golf course (free to play).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free Queenstown Arts & Crafts Market at Earnslaw Park (runs weekends, but check local listings). Walk the free 5km Frankton Arm Walkway along the lake shore for easy, scenic exercise. Visit the free Lake Hayes walking loop nearby if transport is available (~20 min drive).
day_by_day.evening: Queenstown Thursday Night Market on O'Connell's Shopping Centre carpark – free entry, local food stalls (budget ~NZD $15-20 for a full meal from market vendors), live music, and great atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Self-cater – yoghurt, granola, and fresh fruit from Pak'nSave. Budget ~NZD $5.
meals.lunch: Pak'nSave deli or self-catered picnic in the Queenstown Gardens. Budget ~NZD $8.
meals.dinner: Queenstown Thursday Night Market – try local venison sliders, craft beer, or wood-fired pizza from market vendors. Budget ~NZD $15-20.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to plan and book remaining activities for the trip. Consider booking the Nevis Bungy or Shotover Canyon Swing if budget allows for a second adrenaline experience. Check DOC website for any track closures or weather warnings for upcoming hikes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Glenorchy – take the scenic 45-minute drive (or $30 return shuttle) along Lake Wakatipu's western shore to the tiny frontier town of Glenorchy. Stop at all the scenic viewpoints along the way. Arrive and walk the free Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (1 hour loop) through wetlands with stunning mountain backdrops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the free Paradise Track near Glenorchy – a flat, easy walk through the iconic Paradise Valley (filming location for Lord of the Rings). Explore the beech forest and river flats. Return to Queenstown in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Queenstown. Walk the free Queenstown Bay waterfront trail at sunset. Grab a cheap takeaway dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-cater at accommodation. Budget ~NZD $5.
meals.lunch: Glenorchy Café – simple, hearty meals in a classic Kiwi setting, ~NZD $15-18. Or pack your own lunch from Queenstown.
meals.dinner: Burger Wisconsin on the Mall – reliable, affordable burgers from ~NZD $14-16

day_by_day.notes: The Queenstown to Glenorchy road (State Highway 6 / Glenorchy-Queenstown Road) is one of the most scenic drives in New Zealand – stop at the Lake Dispute lookout and Bennetts Bluff lookout. If hiring a car for this day (~NZD $50-60 from Queenstown), you can access more remote Paradise Valley tracks.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Arrowtown – take the Connectabus or Ritchies bus (~NZD $5 each way) to the charming historic gold-mining village 20 minutes from Queenstown. Visit the free Arrow River historic precinct and walk the main street of heritage buildings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the free Arrow River Bridges Track (3.5 hours return, 10km) – a beautiful trail following the Arrow River through a narrow gorge with five historic swing bridges. Alternatively, pan for gold at the river (free activity, borrow a pan from local shops for ~NZD $5).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for the Queenstown Saturday Night Market or a relaxed dinner. Plan the second week of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Self-cater. Budget ~NZD $5.
meals.lunch: Provisions of Arrowtown on Buckingham Street – excellent coffee and cabinet food, ~NZD $12-15
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant is nearby but pricey – instead try Bao Now on Camp Street in Queenstown for affordable Asian-fusion bao buns ~NZD $14-18

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown is a free and fascinating destination. The Lakes District Museum in Arrowtown is worth the ~NZD $10 entry fee for gold-rush history. The autumn colours Arrowtown is famous for are a March-May phenomenon, but November still offers lovely green scenery along the Arrow River.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Wanaka (1.5 hours from Queenstown via Crown Range Road – the highest sealed road in NZ). Take the InterCity bus (~NZD $15-20 one way) or join a budget day tour. Walk the free Wanaka Lakefront Promenade and see the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' – a lone willow growing in the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the free Diamond Lake and Rocky Mountain Track (3-4 hours return) near Wanaka – a spectacular loop with panoramic views of Lake Wanaka and Mount Aspiring. Or explore the free Outlet Track along the Clutha River.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown by evening bus. Grab dinner near the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-cater before departure. Budget ~NZD $5.
meals.lunch: Relishes Café in Wanaka – great value cabinet food and meals, ~NZD $14-18. Or pack lunch from Queenstown.
meals.dinner: Vudu Café & Larder in Queenstown for a reliable, affordable dinner ~NZD $18-22

day_by_day.notes: The Crown Range Road is scenic but has steep grades and sharp corners – if taking a bus, sit on the right side for the best views. Check InterCity bus timetables in advance at intercity.co.nz. Wanaka is a wonderful, slightly quieter alternative to Queenstown and well worth the day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Milford Sound / Piopiotahi – the most iconic destination in New Zealand. Depart Queenstown very early (~6:00am) on an affordable day tour bus (~NZD $80-120 including cruise, book with Real NZ or Jucy Cruize for best budget rates). The drive through Fiordland is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Milford Sound (~11:30am). Board the included 2-hour Milford Sound cruise – see Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, Bowen Falls, seals, penguins, and dolphins. The scenery is absolutely breathtaking and unlike anywhere else on Earth.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Queenstown, arriving back ~8:00-9:00pm. It's a long day (14-15 hours) but absolutely worth it. Grab a late dinner or snack on return.

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast before 6:00am departure – energy bars, banana, coffee in a thermos. Budget ~NZD $5.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from Pak'nSave to eat on the bus or at Milford Sound – saves significant money vs. onsite café. Budget ~NZD $8.
meals.dinner: Late return – Fergbaker bakery stays open late and offers affordable pies and hot food ~NZD $8-10

day_by_day.notes: Book the Milford Sound day tour at least 3-5 days in advance, especially in November (peak season). Compare prices at bookme.co.nz for last-minute deals. The Homer Tunnel on the road to Milford is an engineering marvel – watch for kea (alpine parrots) at the tunnel entrance. Bring rain gear as Milford Sound receives over 7 metres of rain annually, even in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest after the Milford Sound marathon day. Sleep in, have a slow breakfast, and do any trip admin. Visit the free Queenstown waterfront gardens and lakeside area for gentle morning exercise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free Queenstown Trail network – rent a bike (~NZD $35-45/half day from Around the Basin or Vertigo Bikes) and cycle the easy Queenstown Trail along Lake Hayes or the Arrow River. This is a beautiful, flat, scenic ride suitable for all fitness levels.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a lakefront bar. Try Minus 5 Ice Bar for a unique experience (~NZD $30 includes a cocktail) or enjoy free sunset views from the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Self-cater – big recovery breakfast. Eggs, toast, fruit juice. Budget ~NZD $7.
meals.lunch: Self-catered picnic on the bike trail. Budget ~NZD $8.
meals.dinner: The Fishbone Bar & Grill on Beach Street – fresh New Zealand fish and chips at the bar, ~NZD $20-25

day_by_day.notes: The Queenstown Trail is a DOC-managed free cycling and walking trail network. Bike hire is the main cost. Alternatively, the lakefront section of the trail is easily walkable for free. Check the Queenstown Trail website at queenstowntrail.co.nz for maps and route options.

day_by_day.morning: Second bungee or adrenaline experience day – choose based on budget. Option A: Nevis Bungy (134m, the highest in NZ, ~NZD $275) for the ultimate thrill. Option B: Shotover Canyon Swing (~NZD $199) – a unique freefall swing experience. Option C: Queenstown Luge on Bob's Peak (~NZD $45 for 3 rides including gondola) for a more budget-friendly thrill.
day_by_day.afternoon: If energy allows, hike the free One Mile Creek Track from central Queenstown (2 hours return) through native bush. Or visit the free Queenstown waterfront and rent a kayak (~NZD $25/hour from Queenstown Bike Hire) on Lake Wakatipu.
day_by_day.evening: Final big night out in Queenstown. Explore the famous Queenstown bar scene on The Mall and Cow Lane. Budget ~NZD $20-30 for drinks.

meals.breakfast: Self-cater. Budget ~NZD $5.
meals.lunch: Devil Burger on the Mall – great value burgers ~NZD $14-16
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant is a splurge option for a special occasion (~NZD $35-45 main) – or keep it budget with Bao Now or Habebe for ~NZD $15-18

day_by_day.notes: If choosing the Nevis Bungy, book well in advance at bungy.co.nz. The Nevis requires a shuttle to the bungy platform in the Nevis Valley – allow a full morning. All AJ Hackett experiences include a free shuttle from central Queenstown. Check for combo deals if doing multiple AJ Hackett activities during the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final full hiking day – tackle the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (2.5 hours return) if not done earlier in the trip, or revisit a favourite section of the Ben Lomond track for a shorter version. Alternatively, take the free Kelvin Heights Peninsula Walk (1.5 hours return) along the lake for gentle morning exercise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Queenstown Arts & Crafts Market (Saturdays/Sundays) or browse the affordable shops on the Mall. Visit Pak'nSave for New Zealand food souvenirs (Whittaker's chocolate, Pic's peanut butter, Manuka honey) at supermarket prices.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Queenstown. Reflect on the incredible 13 days of hiking and adventure. Pack bags for departure.

meals.breakfast: Self-cater – use up remaining food supplies. Budget ~NZD $5.
meals.lunch: Fergbaker – one last iconic Queenstown pie. Budget ~NZD $8.
meals.dinner: The Cow Restaurant on Cow Lane – a Queenstown institution, perfect for a memorable farewell meal. Pasta or pizza ~NZD $22-26.

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing this evening. Check airline baggage allowances – if you've purchased souvenirs, ensure bags are within limits. Confirm departure logistics: Connectabus to Queenstown Airport costs ~NZD $10 and takes 20-25 minutes. Check bus timetables in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the Queenstown Bay waterfront – completely free and absolutely beautiful. Grab a farewell flat white from a local café (New Zealand coffee culture is exceptional – budget ~NZD $5-6).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Queenstown Boutique Stay (standard checkout 10:00-11:00am). Store luggage at the accommodation if needed. Take one final walk through central Queenstown. Head to Queenstown Airport via Connectabus (~NZD $10) in time for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Queenstown – end of an incredible 13-day South Island adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered or café breakfast. Try a classic New Zealand flat white and a filled croissant from a local café. Budget ~NZD $10-12.
meals.lunch: Airport café or pack snacks for the flight. Budget ~NZD $10-15.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at least 90 minutes before domestic departure or 2 hours before international departure. Queenstown Airport is small but can get busy in peak season. Return any rented gear before heading to the airport. Dispose of any fresh food items before airport security. New Zealand has strict biosecurity – declare all food items or face significant fines.

trip_options.title: Classic New Zealand South Island Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Transfer to Queenstown Boutique Stay, check in, and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along the Queenstown waterfront and Lake Wakatipu promenade to get your bearings and soak in the stunning mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore central Queenstown's vibrant Steamer Wharf precinct. Browse the shops along the Mall and enjoy the lively atmosphere of this adventure capital.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Queenstown Airport or a nearby café upon arrival — try Vudu Café & Larder for fresh sandwiches and coffee (~NZD 15–20)
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant on The Mall — a mid-range gem from chef Josh Emett offering seasonal New Zealand cuisine with locally sourced ingredients (~NZD 40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light to allow for jet lag recovery and orientation. Pick up any hiking supplies or rental gear you may need from the central Queenstown outdoor shops (Kathmandu, Macpac) this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Ben Lomond Summit Hike — Start early (7:30 AM) from central Queenstown. Take the Skyline Gondola up to the Skyline complex (optional, saves ~1 hour) then follow the Ben Lomond Track through tussock and alpine terrain to the 1,748m summit. Allow 5–7 hours total for the full hike. Enjoy panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, The Remarkables, and Cecil Peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ben Lomond Summit Hike descent back to Queenstown (the hike occupies most of the day). Return to town by mid-to-late afternoon. Stop at the Skyline Gondola complex for a rest and views on the way down.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover at the hotel. Enjoy a relaxing dinner in Queenstown town center.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or pick up supplies from a local supermarket/café — Patagonia Chocolates café offers great pastries and coffee (~NZD 10–15)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — prepare sandwiches, trail mix, and energy bars the night before
meals.dinner: Fergburger — Queenstown's legendary burger institution, a must-visit for every traveler. Expect a queue but worth it (~NZD 15–20)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy hiking boots and bring layers — weather can change rapidly above the treeline on Ben Lomond. Carry at least 2 liters of water. Check the Department of Conservation (DOC) website for track conditions before departure. Gondola ticket costs approximately NZD 32 one-way.

day_by_day.morning: Active recovery morning — sleep in slightly, then enjoy a gentle walk along the Queenstown Gardens loop track (~3km, 45 minutes). Explore the rose gardens and lakeside paths at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nevis Bungy Jump — Book the 13:00 or 14:00 session with AJ Hackett. Transfer by 4WD bus to the Nevis Valley site (~45 minutes from Queenstown). Experience New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters with an 8.5-second freefall over the dramatic Nevis River gorge. Return transfer brings you back to Queenstown by approximately 17:00.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your Nevis jump with drinks and dinner in Queenstown. Browse your jump photos and video package at the AJ Hackett retail store.

meals.breakfast: Eichardt's Bar — elegant brunch in a heritage hotel setting overlooking the lake (~NZD 20–30)
meals.lunch: Winnies Gourmet Pizza Bar on The Mall — great wood-fired pizzas in a relaxed setting (~NZD 20–25)
meals.dinner: Pub on Wharf at Steamer Wharf — lively atmosphere with hearty New Zealand pub fare, craft beers, and lake views (~NZD 30–40)

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy costs approximately NZD 275 per person. Book at least 24–48 hours in advance, especially in the November shoulder-season. Weight restrictions apply (45–127kg). Wear comfortable, close-fitting clothing. The photo/video package is an extra ~NZD 99 but highly recommended as a memento.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Glenorchy (45 minutes from Queenstown along the stunning Lake Wakatipu road). Stop at multiple scenic lookouts along the way. Arrive in Glenorchy and explore this charming small town — the gateway to the Routeburn and Greenstone Tracks. Walk the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (~1 hour, easy flat track through wetlands with mountain reflections).
day_by_day.afternoon: Routeburn Track Day Hike — Begin the Routeburn Track from the Glenorchy end (Routeburn Shelter trailhead). Hike to Routeburn Flats and Routeburn Falls (~4–5 hours return, 16km). This world-class Great Walk section offers beech forest, open river flats, cascading waterfalls, and dramatic alpine views toward Mount Aspiring National Park.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Queenstown along the scenic Lake Wakatipu road, stopping at the Twelve Mile Delta recreation reserve for a sunset photo over the lake.

meals.breakfast: Vudu Café & Larder in Queenstown before departure (~NZD 15–20)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Routeburn Track — prepare the night before; there are beautiful spots at Routeburn Flats for a picnic
meals.dinner: Bespoke Kitchen in Queenstown — wholesome, seasonal café-style dinner with great vegetarian and meat options (~NZD 25–35)

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track day hike does not require a Great Walk pass for day visitors — only overnight hut users need to book. Wear waterproof layers as conditions can be unpredictable. The drive from Queenstown to Glenorchy is itself one of the most scenic roads in New Zealand — allow extra time for photo stops.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown toward Te Anau (2 hours). Stop at the Kingston Flyer historic railway site and enjoy the pastoral scenery of the Southland plains. Arrive in Te Anau — the gateway to Fiordland National Park. Check out the Te Anau glowworm caves (Real Journeys tour, ~2 hours, book in advance) for a magical underground experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Te Anau township and the lakefront. Walk the Te Anau Lakefront Walkway (~2km, flat and scenic). Visit the Fiordland National Park Visitor Centre to learn about the region's ecology and Maori history. Begin the scenic drive toward Milford Sound along the Milford Road (SH94) — one of the world's most scenic drives.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Te Anau for the night (staying overnight in Te Anau or continuing to Queenstown — this itinerary keeps you mobile with Queenstown as base, so return drive is 2 hours). Alternatively, book a Te Anau guesthouse for a more relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Queenstown or packed breakfast for the road
meals.lunch: The Sandfly Café in Te Anau — a beloved local institution with great pies, soups, and cabinet food (~NZD 15–20)
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau — rustic, cozy atmosphere serving Fiordland venison, salmon, and local produce (~NZD 35–50)

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour costs approximately NZD 85 per adult and must be pre-booked through Real Journeys. This is a preparatory day for the Milford Sound experience tomorrow. If staying overnight in Te Anau, book accommodation in advance as it fills quickly in November.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Sound Guided Walk and Cruise — Depart Te Anau or Queenstown early (coaches depart ~7:00 AM from Queenstown). Drive the spectacular Milford Road through the Homer Tunnel. Begin the guided nature walk along a section of the Milford Track, with an expert guide explaining the unique Fiordland rainforest ecosystem, waterfalls, and wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the Milford Sound scenic cruise (~2 hours). Cruise through the dramatic fiord flanked by Mitre Peak (1,692m) and sheer granite walls draped in waterfalls. Look for Fiordland crested penguins, fur seals, and bottlenose dolphins. Disembark and return journey begins.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown by coach or private vehicle (arriving approximately 19:30–20:00). Rest at the hotel after a long but spectacular day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure or en route
meals.lunch: Milford Sound Lodge café or packed lunch — most cruise operators offer onboard light refreshments; a packed lunch is recommended for the guided walk portion (~NZD 15–20 if purchasing at Milford)
meals.dinner: The Bunker Restaurant in Queenstown — intimate, cozy restaurant with excellent New Zealand lamb and venison in a warm cabin atmosphere (~NZD 40–55)

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Sound Guided Walk and Cruise package costs approximately NZD 180–220 per person through operators like Real Journeys or Go Orange. Book well in advance for November. Sandflies are notorious at Milford Sound — bring strong insect repellent. Waterproof jacket is essential regardless of forecast.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Queenstown. Sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Visit the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (~2.5 hours, moderate, 400m elevation gain) for panoramic views over the town and lake — a less-demanding alternative to Ben Lomond.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Queenstown Arts & Crafts Market (held at Earnslaw Park on weekends) for local artisan goods, food stalls, and live music. Visit the Kiwi Birdlife Park for a close encounter with kiwi birds, tuatara, and native New Zealand wildlife (~NZD 55 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely evening exploring Queenstown's nightlife and entertainment precinct around Beach Street and The Mall.

meals.breakfast: Bespoke Kitchen — avocado toast, eggs, and specialty coffee in a relaxed setting (~NZD 20–25)
meals.lunch: Queenstown Arts & Crafts Market food stalls — sample local cheeses, artisan bread, venison pies, and fresh produce (~NZD 15–25)
meals.dinner: Flame Bar & Grill at Steamer Wharf — excellent New Zealand beef steaks and fresh South Island salmon with lake views (~NZD 35–50)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally relaxed as a midpoint recovery day. Use this afternoon to do laundry, restock trail supplies, and plan the second half of the trip. The Kiwi Birdlife Park kiwi encounters are typically in the afternoon — check their show times upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Wanaka (1 hour via the Crown Range Road — New Zealand's highest sealed road, with spectacular panoramic views). Stop at the Crown Range Summit lookout for photos. Arrive in Wanaka and explore the charming lakeside town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Roys Peak Track — Begin this iconic hike from the Roys Peak trailhead (5km from Wanaka town). The 16km return hike (5–6 hours) climbs 1,578m through open farmland and tussock to a ridge with arguably the most photographed view in New Zealand — Lake Wanaka with Mount Aspiring in the background. Start no later than 12:00 PM for afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka town. Relax by the lakefront at Wanaka's famous 'That Wanaka Tree' (a lone willow tree growing from the lake). Drive back to Queenstown (1 hour) or stay overnight in Wanaka.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Queenstown before departure — Federal Diner for a hearty full breakfast (~NZD 20–25)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Roys Peak Track — the summit ridge offers a spectacular picnic spot
meals.dinner: Ritual Café in Wanaka (if staying overnight) or The Cow Restaurant in Queenstown upon return — famous for fondue and pizza in a stone cottage (~NZD 25–35)

day_by_day.notes: Roys Peak Track is closed from October 1 to November 10 for lambing season — by November 22 it should be fully open. Confirm with DOC before departure. The track is steep and exposed — bring sunscreen, plenty of water (2L+), and wind-proof layers. The summit view is best in clear weather; check the forecast the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown/Wanaka south toward the Catlins region OR explore the Arrowtown area. Take the scenic Arrow River Trail from Arrowtown (~2 hours, easy riverside walk through historic gold-mining country). Explore Arrowtown's beautifully preserved 19th-century gold rush main street and Chinese settlement.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown. Try an afternoon Shotover Jet boat experience on the Shotover River Canyon (~NZD 155) — a thrilling 25-minute ride through narrow rock canyons at high speed, a perfect complement to the bungy jump experience.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Queenstown. Visit the Queenstown Night Market (held Thursday–Sunday on Earnslaw Park) for street food from around the world.

meals.breakfast: Provisions of Arrowtown — a beautiful artisan café in a heritage building with excellent eggs and baked goods (~NZD 20–25)
meals.lunch: Arrowtown Bakery — legendary meat pies and filled rolls in the heart of historic Arrowtown (~NZD 12–18)
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market — sample diverse street food from Thai, Indian, Mexican, and New Zealand stalls (~NZD 20–30)

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown is only 20 minutes from Queenstown and is one of the most charming historic towns in New Zealand — highly recommended. The Shotover Jet is a separate adventure activity that pairs well with the bungy jump for thrill-seekers. Book Shotover Jet online in advance for a slight discount.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Fiordland for a different perspective — head to Doubtful Sound via Manapouri (3 hours from Queenstown). Alternatively, explore the Kepler Track day hike near Te Anau. For this itinerary: drive to Te Anau and begin the Kepler Track from the Te Anau control gates. Hike to the Brod Bay campsite and along the lakeside (~3 hours return, easy to moderate).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Kepler Track up toward the Luxmore Hut if energy allows (adds ~3 hours, steep but rewarding alpine views). Alternatively, return to Te Anau and explore the Te Anau Bird Sanctuary — a free outdoor aviary with takahe and other endangered New Zealand birds.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Queenstown (2 hours). Enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel with dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Vudu Café before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Kepler Track — eat at Brod Bay beside the lake for a stunning setting
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant in Queenstown — revisit this excellent establishment or try Bazaar Interactive Marketplace Restaurant at the Hilton for an international buffet experience (~NZD 55–65)

day_by_day.notes: The Kepler Track is a Great Walk but day visitors do not need hut passes. The lakeside section to Brod Bay is one of the most accessible and beautiful sections of any Great Walk in New Zealand. November weather in Fiordland can be unpredictable — always carry rain gear.

day_by_day.morning: Full day excursion to Mount Cook / Aoraki National Park (3.5 hours from Queenstown via Lake Pukaki). The drive along the Mackenzie Basin with turquoise Lake Pukaki and Aoraki/Mount Cook (3,724m — New Zealand's highest peak) in the background is breathtaking. Stop at the Lake Pukaki viewpoint for iconic photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hooker Valley Track — New Zealand's most popular alpine walk (10km return, 3 hours, easy). Walk through glacial moraines and across swing bridges to the Hooker Glacier terminal lake with floating icebergs and direct views of Aoraki/Mount Cook's south face. A world-class, accessible alpine experience.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Queenstown (3.5 hours). Alternatively, stay overnight at Mount Cook Village for stargazing in one of New Zealand's darkest sky reserves (the Aoraki Mackenzie International Dark Sky Reserve is world-renowned).

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure (~NZD 15–20 or included)
meals.lunch: Old Mountaineers' Café in Mount Cook Village — legendary café with hearty soups, pies, and the best views of any café in New Zealand (~NZD 20–30)
meals.dinner: If returning to Queenstown: Sherwood Restaurant — farm-to-table dining with organic, local ingredients in a relaxed lodge setting (~NZD 35–50). If staying at Mount Cook: The Panorama Room at The Hermitage Hotel (~NZD 60–80)

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is graded easy and suitable for all fitness levels — a wonderful contrast to the more challenging hikes earlier in the trip. November is an excellent time for Mount Cook as snow conditions on the lower tracks are usually manageable. Bring warm layers regardless of Queenstown weather — Mount Cook is significantly colder.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day in Queenstown. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely morning. Visit the Queenstown Gondola for breakfast at the Stratosfare Restaurant (~NZD 35 with gondola) and enjoy the morning views over the lake and The Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore any remaining Queenstown experiences — consider a wine tour of the Gibbston Valley wine region (20 minutes from Queenstown), known for world-class Pinot Noir. The Gibbston Valley Winery cave tour and tasting is a unique underground experience (~NZD 30 for tasting). Alternatively, take a scenic cruise on the TSS Earnslaw steamship across Lake Wakatipu to Walter Peak High Country Farm (~NZD 85).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Queenstown. Revisit a favorite restaurant or try somewhere new. Take a final evening walk along the Queenstown waterfront to watch the last light fade over The Remarkables.

meals.breakfast: Stratosfare Restaurant at the Queenstown Gondola — buffet breakfast with panoramic views (~NZD 35 including gondola)
meals.lunch: Gibbston Valley Winery Restaurant — seasonal menu paired with estate Pinot Noir in a stunning schist-stone setting (~NZD 35–45)
meals.dinner: Fishbone Bar & Grill — Queenstown's premier seafood restaurant featuring fresh South Island salmon, blue cod, and Bluff oysters (~NZD 40–55)

day_by_day.notes: The Gibbston Valley wine region is often called the 'Valley of the Vines' and is the southernmost wine-producing region in the world. November is the beginning of the growing season — the vines will be lush and green. Book the winery restaurant for lunch in advance. This is your last full day — use the evening to pack and prepare for departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Enjoy a slow, relaxed breakfast. Take a last walk through the Queenstown Gardens or along the lakefront. Check out of Queenstown Boutique Stay (standard check-out is 10:00–11:00 AM — confirm with hotel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: if afternoon flight, head to the airport with time to browse the Queenstown Airport duty-free shops and pick up New Zealand souvenirs (Manuka honey, Whittaker's chocolate, merino wool products). If morning flight, depart directly after breakfast.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Queenstown Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of hiking, adventure, and natural beauty across the South Island.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a Queenstown café — Vudu Café & Larder for a nostalgic bookend to the trip (~NZD 15–20)
meals.lunch: Airport café or packed snacks for the journey
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for check-in at Queenstown Airport, especially for international connections. The airport is only 10 minutes from central Queenstown. Consider purchasing travel insurance claims for any weather-affected activities before departure. Queenstown Airport has limited luggage storage if you need to store bags after check-out.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
experiences.description: One of New Zealand's most iconic day hikes, crossing volcanic terrain with stunning views of emerald lakes and craters. Book an early shuttle from Queenstown or Wanaka to maximize daylight hours. Ideal for Day 2 or 3 after a rested arrival. Stay in Taupo or National Park Village the night before to avoid long morning transfers.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters, operated by AJ Hackett. Located just outside Queenstown, this is a must-do for adrenaline seekers. Book in advance to secure your preferred time slot. Stay in central Queenstown to minimize transfer time — the jump site is a short bus ride from town.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: A world-class Great Walk offering breathtaking alpine scenery through Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The Routeburn Falls and Lake Harris sections are accessible as a day hike. Stay in Glenorchy (45 min from Queenstown) the night before to catch the early morning trailhead shuttle and avoid wasted travel time.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Guided Walk and Cruise
experiences.description: Combine a guided nature walk along the Milford Track with a scenic cruise through Milford Sound's dramatic fiords and waterfalls. Depart from Te Anau (not Queenstown) to cut 1.5 hours off the transfer. Book accommodation in Te Anau the night before this activity to ensure an early, stress-free departure.

experiences.name: Ben Lomond Summit Hike
experiences.description: A challenging full-day hike directly accessible from central Queenstown, reaching 1,748 meters with panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. No transfers needed — the trailhead starts in town via the Skyline gondola area. Perfect for a mid-trip activity day when staying in central Queenstown, keeping costs and logistics minimal.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Private luxury transfer to Queenstown Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the Queenstown waterfront promenade to soak in views of Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at Skyline Queenstown — take the gondola up Bob's Peak for panoramic views over Queenstown at dusk. Ease into your luxury escape with a relaxed first dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy complimentary in-flight meal or light snack on arrival
meals.lunch: Casual welcome lunch at Rata Restaurant — modern New Zealand cuisine by chef Josh Emett, featuring seasonal local produce
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amisfield Winery & Bistro — a celebrated Central Otago winery offering a renowned 'Trust the Chef' degustation menu paired with estate wines

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance with your boutique stay concierge. Allow time to acclimatize and rest after the long-haul flight. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings with the hotel concierge this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel, then head out for a scenic e-bike or walking tour of Queenstown's lakefront and Frankton Arm Trail — a gentle warm-up to get your bearings and enjoy the alpine scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Skyline Gondola up to Bob's Peak and explore the walking tracks above Queenstown, including short trails with sweeping views of Lake Wakatipu. Visit the luge track for a playful premium experience.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset lake cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard a chartered vessel, with champagne and canapés served on deck as the sun dips behind The Remarkables.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Queenstown Boutique Stay — eggs Benedict, fresh-pressed juices, artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sherwood Queenstown — farm-to-table dining with an emphasis on sustainability and local South Island ingredients
meals.dinner: Dinner at Botswana Butchery — a Queenstown institution known for premium aged steaks, fresh seafood, and an extensive wine list overlooking the lake

day_by_day.notes: This is a relaxed orientation day. Use the afternoon and evening to confirm logistics for the Nevis Bungy Jump and Ben Lomond hike later in the week. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Ben Lomond Summit Hike — depart from central Queenstown and ascend via the Tiki Trail and Ben Lomond Saddle. The full hike reaches 1,748 meters with spectacular 360-degree views over Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, and surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the descent at your own pace, arriving back in Queenstown mid-afternoon. Treat yourself to a well-deserved soak and massage at a premium day spa such as the Eforea Spa at Hilton Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Queenstown's vibrant town center. Browse the boutique shops along the Mall before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast box prepared by the hotel — smoked salmon bagels, fruit, energy bars, and a thermos of coffee
meals.lunch: Packed premium trail lunch — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, Otago cherries, chocolate, and electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bunker Restaurant — intimate underground dining room with an exceptional seasonal menu and curated wine list; book well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is a strenuous 8–10 hour hike with approximately 1,400m of elevation gain. Wear sturdy hiking boots, carry sunscreen, and bring plenty of water. Check weather conditions the evening before and be prepared to reschedule if alpine weather is poor.

day_by_day.morning: Active recovery morning — gentle yoga or Pilates session arranged through the hotel, followed by a swim in the pool. Take time to journal and enjoy the mountain views from the boutique stay's terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Arrowtown — a charming historic gold-mining village 20 minutes from Queenstown. Explore the Chinese Settlement, the Lakes District Museum, and the picturesque Arrowtown main street lined with heritage stone buildings and boutique galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting tour through the Gibbston Valley — the 'Valley of the Vines' — visiting two or three premium Central Otago wineries such as Peregrine, Chard Farm, and Gibbston Valley Winery, famous for Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel — avocado toast, house-made granola, freshly squeezed orange juice, and flat whites
meals.lunch: Lunch at Provisions of Arrowtown — a beloved local café with outstanding cabinet food, house-baked bread, and excellent coffee
meals.dinner: Dinner at Gibbston Valley Winery's Cave Restaurant — a unique dining experience inside a natural schist rock cave, paired with estate Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private driver or luxury vehicle for the Gibbston Valley wine tour so you can enjoy the tastings responsibly. This is a wonderful recovery day after the Ben Lomond hike.

day_by_day.morning: The moment of truth — Nevis Bungy Jump! Transfer via AJ Hackett's private 4WD vehicles into the Nevis Valley. Prepare for New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters, suspended above the Nevis River gorge. A truly bucket-list adrenaline experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown and celebrate your jump! Collect your professional photos and video package from AJ Hackett. Unwind with a riverside walk along the Kawarau Gorge or visit the historic Kawarau Bridge — the world's first commercial bungy site.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory evening in Queenstown — cocktails at a rooftop bar followed by a premium dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Light but energizing breakfast at the hotel — do not eat too heavily before the jump. Fresh fruit, yogurt, and toast recommended
meals.lunch: Post-jump celebratory lunch at Fergburger (a Queenstown institution) or a sit-down meal at Hawthorne Coffee House for gourmet burgers and craft beer
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at Queenstown's Rata Restaurant — refined New Zealand cuisine with local lamb, venison, and fresh seafood in an elegant setting

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires a minimum weight of 45kg and maximum of 127kg. Participants must sign a health and safety waiver. Avoid alcohol the night before. The experience includes transport, harness fitting, and a commemorative certificate. Purchase the photo/video package for lasting memories.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown for the Routeburn Track Day Hike — a private guided experience with a certified alpine guide. Drive to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead near Glenorchy (approximately 1 hour from Queenstown). Begin hiking through ancient beech forest toward the Routeburn Flats and Routeburn Falls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided hike up to Lake Harris (2,000m) if conditions allow, enjoying extraordinary views of the Harris Saddle and surrounding Fiordland peaks. This world-class Great Walk section showcases some of the most dramatic alpine scenery in New Zealand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown via Glenorchy Road — one of New Zealand's most scenic drives along Lake Wakatipu. Stop at a lakeside viewpoint for a sundowner drink.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast at the hotel — eggs your way, smoked salmon, fresh fruit, and strong coffee before the drive
meals.lunch: Premium packed trail lunch provided by the hotel or guide — antipasto selection, local cheeses, crackers, fruit, and energy snacks
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pier 19 Restaurant in Queenstown — relaxed lakeside dining with fresh South Island seafood and an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track day hike is approximately 16–20km return depending on how far you go. Wear waterproof hiking boots and carry rain gear — Fiordland weather can change rapidly. A private guide enhances the experience with ecological and cultural commentary. Book guide in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic helicopter flight over Fiordland and Milford Sound — a premium 45-minute to 1-hour flight departing from Queenstown, offering aerial views of the Southern Alps, glaciers, and the dramatic Fiordland coastline. Some tours include a glacier landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown for a relaxed afternoon. Visit the Queenstown Art Gallery or browse the boutique shops. Optional: kayak on Lake Wakatipu with a guided luxury kayak experience.
day_by_day.evening: Twilight Queenstown food and wine walk — a guided premium culinary tour of Queenstown's best restaurants, bars, and artisan producers, sampling local cheeses, wines, craft beers, and small plates.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the hotel — croissants, house-made preserves, seasonal fruit, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Vudu Café & Larder — Queenstown's favorite café for house-baked breads, fresh salads, and exceptional coffee
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kō Restaurant at The Rees Hotel — a lakeside fine dining experience with a focus on indigenous Māori ingredients and contemporary New Zealand cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter flights are weather-dependent — confirm on the morning of departure. Book through Glacier Southern Lakes Helicopters or Over The Top Helicopters for the most premium experience. The food and wine walk should be booked in advance through Queenstown Wine Trail or a similar operator.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Queenstown for Te Anau (approximately 2 hours by private luxury vehicle). Check in to a premium Te Anau lodge — recommended: Te Anau Lodge or Fiordland Lodge — before heading out to explore the lakefront town of Te Anau, the gateway to Fiordland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Te Anau Glowworm Caves boat tour — a magical underground experience through ancient limestone caves filled with thousands of tiny glowworms (Arachnocampa luminosa), accessible only by boat across Lake Te Anau.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Te Anau lakefront, watching the light fade over the Fiordland mountains reflected in the still waters of Lake Te Anau.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at Queenstown Boutique Stay before checking out and driving to Te Anau
meals.lunch: Lunch at Miles Better Pies or The Fat Duck Restaurant in Te Anau — casual but high-quality local dining
meals.dinner: Dinner at Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau — a beloved local institution in a heritage cottage, offering venison, lamb, and fresh Fiordland seafood

day_by_day.notes: This is a transition day from Queenstown to Te Anau. Confirm your premium accommodation in Te Anau in advance. The Glowworm Caves tour must be booked ahead through Real Journeys. Pack bags carefully as you will be based in Te Anau for two nights before moving to Milford Sound.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Sound Guided Walk and Cruise — depart Te Anau early for the 2-hour drive along the spectacular Milford Road through Homer Tunnel. Begin a guided nature walk along a section of the legendary Milford Track, exploring ancient rainforest, waterfalls, and glacial valleys with an expert naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a premium small-group cruise through Milford Sound — New Zealand's most famous fiord. Witness the sheer 1,200-meter cliffs of Mitre Peak, cascading waterfalls including Stirling Falls (151m), and abundant wildlife including fur seals, penguins, and dolphins.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Te Anau along the Milford Road at golden hour — the light on the mountains and lakes is extraordinary. Optional: overnight stay at Milford Sound Lodge for an even more immersive experience.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast from your Te Anau lodge — muffins, fruit, yogurt, and a flask of coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Premium picnic lunch on the Milford Track or light refreshments aboard the cruise vessel
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Sandfly Café or Pio Pio Restaurant in Te Anau — hearty post-adventure dining with local lamb, salmon, and craft beers

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound receives the highest rainfall in New Zealand — rain actually enhances the experience as hundreds of temporary waterfalls appear on the cliff faces. Pack full waterproof gear, insect repellent (sandflies are notorious), and layers. Book the guided walk and cruise package through Real Journeys or Trips & Tramps for the most premium small-group experience.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Te Anau back toward Queenstown, stopping at the Mirror Lakes and Eglinton Valley for photography — some of the most stunning reflective lake scenery in New Zealand. Continue to Wanaka (approximately 2.5 hours from Te Anau via Queenstown).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Wanaka and check in to a premium lakeside property — recommended: Edgewater Hotel or a luxury private villa on Lake Wanaka's shores. Explore the charming Wanaka township and stroll along the famous lakefront with views of Mount Aspiring.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the iconic 'That Wanaka Tree' — a lone willow tree growing from the edge of Lake Wanaka — for sunset photography. Enjoy a relaxed first evening in this beautiful alpine town.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at Te Anau lodge before departing
meals.lunch: Lunch stop at a scenic lakeside spot en route — or dine at Federal Diner in Wanaka upon arrival, a beloved local spot for gourmet café food
meals.dinner: Dinner at Francesca's Italian Kitchen in Wanaka — widely regarded as one of the best restaurants in the South Island, with handmade pasta and exceptional Italian-inspired dishes

day_by_day.notes: Wanaka is a quieter, more relaxed alternative to Queenstown with equally spectacular scenery. The drive via the Eglinton Valley is stunning — allow extra time for stops. Confirm Wanaka accommodation well in advance as premium properties book out quickly in November (peak season).

day_by_day.morning: Roy's Peak Track — one of the most iconic hikes in New Zealand. Depart early from Wanaka for this 8–10 hour return hike (16km, 1,280m elevation gain) to the summit of Roy's Peak at 1,578 meters, with breathtaking panoramic views of Lake Wanaka and Mount Aspiring National Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the descent and return to Wanaka. Reward yourself with a cold craft beer at a local brewery or a refreshing swim in Lake Wanaka.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Wanaka — visit Puzzling World for a quirky end-of-day experience, or simply enjoy the sunset from the lakefront with a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast from the hotel — energy-dense foods such as porridge, eggs, bananas, and coffee before the hike
meals.lunch: Packed premium trail lunch — smoked salmon wraps, local cheeses, nuts, dried fruit, and chocolate
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ritual Café or Bistro Gentil in Wanaka — Bistro Gentil offers a sophisticated fine dining experience in a garden setting with French-influenced New Zealand cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Roy's Peak is best started before 7:00am to avoid crowds at the famous 'Instagram ridge' viewpoint and to complete the hike before afternoon heat. Carry at least 2 liters of water per person. Trekking poles are recommended. Check weather conditions the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic flight over Mount Aspiring National Park and the Southern Alps — depart from Wanaka Airport for a breathtaking 1-hour fixed-wing or helicopter scenic flight over glaciers, remote peaks, and pristine wilderness. Aspiring Helicopters or Wanaka Flightseeing offer exceptional premium options.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back to Queenstown (approximately 1 hour) and check back in to Queenstown Boutique Stay. Spend the afternoon at leisure — visit the Queenstown Gardens, browse the Saturday market (if applicable), or enjoy a final lakeside walk.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell luxury experience — private jet boat ride through the Shotover Canyon at sunset, followed by a special farewell dinner at Queenstown's finest restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Wanaka accommodation before checking out
meals.lunch: Lunch at Yonder Restaurant in Queenstown — a creative, plant-forward menu with outstanding local ingredients and a relaxed, stylish atmosphere
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Amisfield Winery & Bistro — the full 'Trust the Chef' degustation experience with premium wine pairings, celebrating an incredible 13-day South Island adventure

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return to Queenstown Boutique Stay and ensure your room is held. The Shotover Jet must be booked in advance. This is a perfect penultimate day combining aerial adventure, reflection, and a memorable farewell dining experience. Begin packing and organizing luggage for departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the hotel. Take one last walk along the Queenstown waterfront or up to the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (a shorter 2–3 hour loop with excellent views) if energy and time allow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Queenstown Boutique Stay. Depending on departure flight time, visit the Kiwi Birdlife Park for a final encounter with New Zealand's native wildlife, including the kiwi, kea, and tuatara. Purchase last-minute gifts at the Queenstown artisan market or boutique stores.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Queenstown Airport. Depart New Zealand with extraordinary memories of 13 days of world-class hiking, adrenaline, and luxury across the South Island.

meals.breakfast: Final indulgent breakfast at Queenstown Boutique Stay — the full spread, savored slowly
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Queenstown's Rata Restaurant or a casual bite at Yonder before heading to the airport
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner at a restaurant near the airport depending on flight schedule

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security at Queenstown Airport. Arrange private transfer in advance.
